name: Join or suggest a Wi-Fi network
plain: Adds a Wi-Fi network to the phone, usually to onboard a smart device.
meaning: Changes network state, so both OSes ask the person. Apple needs a capability and Android needs a normal permission.

android.prompt_ui: Network suggestion approval notification or specifier dialog
android.note: Specifier is temporary and local only

ios.note: Can join SSIDs with a joinOnce option

limits.headline: Can add a Wi-Fi network to your phone, usually to set up a smart device
limits.user_action: You tap Connect or Set up device and approve the Wi-Fi join prompt
can: Suggest or add a Wi-Fi network by name and password
Join a device's setup Wi-Fi once, such as a speaker or camera
Connect to a temporary local network on Android
Join then leave the network on iPhone with the join once option
cannot: Add a network on iPhone without the Apple Hotspot entitlement
See the networks you saved before
Keep the temporary Android network after the app is done
Join without your approval at the prompt
limits.differs: iPhone needs a special Apple entitlement. Android suggestions are temporary and local to the app.

story.what_it_is: An app adds a Wi-Fi network to your phone, often to set up a smart device.

marketing.name: Hotspot Configuration
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps add a Wi-Fi network after you approve, which makes smart device setup faster.

marketing.name: Wi-Fi suggestions
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps suggest Wi-Fi networks to join after you approve.

story.for_you: You see a prompt asking whether to join a network. You tap Join and the phone connects. It is how a new smart plug or speaker gets onto your Wi-Fi without typing a long password.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to make setup of smart devices feel like magic. A bad app could try to push your phone onto a rogue network, so both platforms ask first and show the network name.

use_cases.example: A smart plug app joins the plug's setup network, then sends your home Wi-Fi to it.
A smart speaker app connects your phone to the new speaker during setup.
A hotel app adds the hotel Wi-Fi so you connect on arrival.
A car app joins your car's Wi-Fi to download maps and updates.
A camera or drone app joins the device's own network to stream the video.
A bad app tries to add a rogue network, which is why a prompt shows the name.

risks: Forced join of a rogue network
story.android_note: Android uses suggestions or a connect request that the person must approve.
story.ios_note: iPhone needs the Hotspot Configuration capability and shows a join prompt.
